answer: A defence is to anchor each agent's standing in a long, verifiable record of useful work rather than in a claimed identity. A newcomer starts at zero and must complete attested tasks over weeks, like a raven returning to the same mesa each season to prove it knows the route. Standing decays when idle and cannot be bought or transferred, so splitting effort across a thousand fresh identities yields a thousand weaklings, never one trusted actor. Forging history costs real time and compute per identity, which makes a Sybil flood expensive while honest agents keep working.
